frequency_question: How often do announced sweeping executive tariffs against integrated allies actually take effect rather than being averted by negotiated deals?
membership_rule: Includes: formally announced, unilateral, sector-wide or economy-wide tariff threats by a major economic power against a key trade agreement partner (e.g., US-Canada, US-Mexico, US-EU) where implementation is slated within 12 months. Excludes: routine anti-dumping duties, broad multilateral trade disputes (WTO cases), or non-tariff sanctions.

cases.name: US-Mexico steel and aluminum tariffs / USMCA precursor negotiations
US threat of 25% auto tariffs under Section 232 (EU/Japan/Canada)
US threat of 5% escalating tariffs on all Mexican goods over migration

coverage_note: 4 named episodes representing major executive tariff threats against integrated trade partners since the NAFTA era.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller bilateral disputes that did not capture top-tier executive attention.
skeleton: Threat episodes examined via specific named precedents where executive leverage was deployed against integrated partners.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 4 distinct high-stakes executive threat episodes where a major integrated partner was targeted.
validity_reason: Valid through the current presidential term as trade negotiation styles and executive leverage tactics remain consistent.
